correctness.rationale: For C4□Cn with n≥7 the shortest graph distance is d_n+d_4. A clique not contained in adjacent columns must contain two same-row vertices in columns j−1 and j+1 of distance exactly two; every additional vertex is one of three center-column rows r−1,r,r+1. The endpoint pair B_(j,r) is unique for each outside face because no second distance-two pair fits. For each B, the four lower faces B∪T (T⊆{(j,r−1),(j,r+1)}) paired with addition of (j,r), processed in decreasing |T|, are genuinely free and remove all 32n non-slab faces in 16n simplicial collapse steps. Each remaining consecutive-column slab has eight vertices and four mutually disjoint forbidden cross edges, hence the boundary of a 4-cross-polytope, a triangulated S³. Adjacent slabs intersect in full four-vertex tetrahedra, all other and triple intersections empty. Cyclic gluing along these contractible intersections adds n S³ summands and a single S¹. Inclusion-exclusion for slabs gives faces (4n,18n,28n,15n), plus outside binomial counts gives full (4n,22n,40n,27n,4n). The separate independent Python enumeration verified every free pair and face count for n=7,8,9 and the source verifier handles n=7..24; finite checks only corroborate the all-n combinatorial proof.
